spec.title: The lock file: vibe.lock
spec.p: `vibe.lock` is the file vibe writes and you commit: the exact versions the project got. This page explains every field so you can read a diff of it in a pull request and know what changed.

where.title: Where it lives and who writes it
where.p: There is one `vibe.lock` per workspace, at the absolute root, beside the root [manifest](../glossary/index.xml#manifest); members never have their own. `vibe install` and `vibe update` write it; `vibe clean` keeps it; nothing edits it by hand. It is the recorded decision; the dependency tree on disk is only its consequence and can always be rebuilt from it.

meta.title: [meta]

tr.td: the vibe version and the time of the last write; informational
the lock schema; an older vibe refuses a newer schema rather than misreading it
the resolver that produced the graph
the coordinates the manifests asked for directly; the baseline of the freshness check
the resolved language preference and its fallbacks, so a re-install on another machine materialises the same files

meta.p: `root_dependencies` copies the manifest's `[requires.packages]`, so the [lock file](../glossary/index.xml#lock-file) is a self-contained snapshot that needs no manifest to read. Removing a root with `vibe uninstall` drops it from both files; removing a package that is only a transitive dependency is refused with an explanation.

tr.td: the package's kind, for placement and filters
the fingerprint of the package's shippable tree; the identity; verified on every fetch
the name of the registry that answered, from the manifest's list
where and at what git ref the bytes were fetched this time; informational, always the canonical address even when a mirror served
`registry`, `git`, `override` or `path`: which resolution path produced the entry; for `path` the URL field holds the member's folder relative to the root
the resolved dependencies of this package, as exact coordinates
true when an `[[override]]` supplied the package
the active features and subskills recorded for the package
the project files this package's install wrote outside its own folder, so that uninstall can remove exactly them
the address of the registry stub that delegated the package elsewhere, when one was followed; absent otherwise

reading-a-diff.title: Reading a diff
reading-a-diff.p: A changed `version` with a changed `content_hash` is an update. A changed `content_hash` with the same version is impossible in a healthy world: vibe refuses it at fetch time, so if you see it in a diff someone edited the file. A changed `source_url` alone is a [mirror](../glossary/index.xml#mirror) or a host migration and means nothing for the project. A new entry with `source_kind = "override"` is a patch someone applied on purpose and should carry a reason in the commit message.

edge-cases.title: Edge cases and rules
edge-cases.p: An unchanged manifest against an unchanged [lock file](../glossary/index.xml#lock-file) makes `vibe install` skip the resolver entirely: the lock is the answer.

The lock file records no [registry](../glossary/index.xml#registry) [index](../glossary/index.xml#index-registry) and no mirror: reproducing it needs only the [coordinates](../glossary/index.xml#coordinate), the [fingerprints](../glossary/index.xml#fingerprint) and a source that can serve them.
`vibe why <coordinate>` explains from the lock file and the manifests why a package is in the project, or what blocked it.
The file is read strictly: a field vibe does not know is an error, not a warning, so a hand edit or a field from a newer vibe is caught at once.
